title.narrative: Inclusive Community Engagement for Humanitarian Response Prioritization in Baydhaba District.

description.narrative: ltpgtURRO will implement a Community Engagement (CE) exercise in Baydhaba District over an eight month period to conduct a structured, evidence based needs assessment that ensures humanitarian interventions are guided by the priorities and voices of crisis affected communities. The exercise will produce a district level Community Engagement Plan (CEP) for Baydhaba, outlining ranked and costed priorities jointly developed with Area Based Committee (ABC) members, OCHA, ASEP as the lead Community Engagement partner, and other implementing partners working across the flagship districts, including Jamaame and Afmadow. The CEP will include disaggregated participation data by age, gender, disability, and minority status, offering practical guidance for inclusive, equitable, and data driven humanitarian programming. The project will also strengthen participatory planning processes by empowering ABCs and implementing partners to facilitate locally led decision making that ensures the sustained inclusion of marginalized and minority groups in the humanitarian response. The findings of this process will inform the second phase of the SHF flagship allocation by providing community validated, evidence based priorities for implementation.ltbrgtThe CE process will begin with coordination between URRO, ABC members, OCHA, ASEP, and relevant line ministries to confirm the target villages and align implementation approaches across the districts. This will be followed by a refresher training for Community Engagement facilitators, led in collaboration with ASEP, to harmonize methodologies, reinforce ethical and protection standards, and prepare teams for field level engagement.ltbrgtFollowing the training, URRO and ABC teams will conduct community entry activities, including meetings with village leaders, mapping of community structures and strategies, and consultations with village committees in the six target villages: October Village, Raydabaale, Ahmed Gurey, Horseed Village, Dhariiqa Village, and Waaberi Village. These engagements will build trust, introduce the project objectives, and ensure inclusive participation of women, men, youth, persons with disabilities, and minority groups.ltbrgtBuilding on this foundation, URRO and ABC teams will facilitate two rounds of structured community action planning sessions across the six target villages: October Village, Raydabaale, Ahmed Gurey, Horseed Village, Dhariiqa Village, and Waaberi Village. During these sessions, community representatives will identify, discuss, and prioritize their most urgent humanitarian needs. The second round of sessions will allow communities to review, refine, and validate the identified priorities, ensuring accuracy, inclusivity, and local ownership.ltbrgtThe collected information will then be jointly reviewed and analyzed by URRO, ABC, OCHA, and ASEP teams, in coordination with other partners implementing the CE process in Jamaame and Afmadow. Community identified priorities will be compiled, ranked, and costed using transparent criteria such as urgency, severity, feasibility, and potential impact. The resulting district level CEP will be presented during a validation workshop with community representatives and ABC members to confirm that it reflects locally defined priorities and perspectives.ltbrgtThroughout the process, ethical and protection principles, including Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), PSEA, GBV, and Child Protection (CP), will be systematically integrated. Participation of persons with disabilities, minority groups, women, and youth will be actively promoted at every stage.ltbrgtFollowing the validation of the CEP, URRO will facilitate routine weekly coordination and progress meetings with ABC members and key stakeholders, including ASEP and other CE partners, to monitor follow up actions, address emerging issues, and ensure that community priorities continue to inform humanitarian decision making throughout the eight month implementation period.ltbrgtlt/pgt
